name: predict_burn
description: The orbit after one to three burns, worked out with the game's patched conics from this turn's Game Snapshot: up to 4 patches, each with its body, Ap and Pe (m above sea level), inclination, eccentricity, start and end UT, and how it ends (escape, encounter <body>, impact, atmosphere or stable), plus the closest approach to a target body and each burn's estimated burn time. Burns are impulsive, in maneuver-node components (prograde, normal, radial m/s), at ap, pe, altitude, eq_an, eq_dn, eq_nearest, eq_highest, rel_an, rel_dn, closest_approach, a UT or "in <s>". Its block is exec_node: call it to check what a node's burn does before you put it in a plan, instead of working the orbit out yourself. Don't call it for transfer_to, return, tune_pe, deorbit, circularize or land, which plan their own burns, for what to burn to reach an orbit (solve_burn), or for the craft's delta-v (stage_performance).

at.description: When, the next one after the burn before: "ap", "pe", "altitude <m> [ascending|descending]", eq_an, eq_dn, eq_nearest, eq_highest, rel_an, rel_dn or closest_approach (the last three use target), a UT in seconds, or "in <s>" seconds from now.

dv.description: m/s in maneuver-node components; a missing one is 0.

target.description: A body to give the closest approach to; also what rel_an, rel_dn and closest_approach measure from.

name: solve_burn
description: The burn to an orbit goal, from this turn's Game Snapshot: maneuver-node components (prograde, normal, radial m/s), magnitude, burn time, the element reached and the predict_burn result. at: ap, pe, altitude, eq_an, eq_dn, eq_nearest, eq_highest, rel_an, rel_dn, closest_approach or a UT. Goals (altitudes in m above sea level): circularize: at ap or pe; set_ap, set_pe: value; next_patch_pe: value above the next body, at default in 60 s; set_sma: value m from the centre, at default pe; set_ecc: value, at default pe; ellipticize: pe and ap, at default in 60 s; set_inc: value degrees, at default eq_highest; match_plane: target's plane, at the cheaper of rel_an and rel_dn; shift_lan: value degrees, default where the planes cross; resonant: value orbits while target (default this orbit) makes of, at default pe; stationary: synchronous circle; intercept_at: Lambert arc, arrive_ut or tof; exec_node only. Its blocks are change_orbit, circularize, exec_node and tune_pe: call it to budget their burn, then pass the block the goal, or exec_node the node. Don't call it to check a burn (predict_burn) or for the craft's delta-v (stage_performance).

at.description: A word from the description, "altitude <m> [ascending|descending]", a UT in seconds or "in <s>". rel_an, rel_dn and closest_approach use target.

name: stage_performance
description: Each stage's delta-v, thrust-to-weight ratio at a body's surface gravity, Isp, burn time, thrust and start and end mass, plus totals, in vacuum or at that body's sea-level pressure, worked out from the craft's stage figures in this turn's Game Snapshot (a stage the stock readout shows as 0 at a trickle throttle is recomputed with the rocket equation). SI units: m/s, s, N, kg. Its blocks are the ones that burn (launch, ascend, land, deorbit, return and the rest): call it to check the craft against a leg's delta-v budget, or a launch's or landing's TWR, and what each stage holds before you shed tanks with drop_empty, instead of working the rocket equation out yourself. Don't call it for where a burn leaves the orbit, or again when the craft hasn't changed since you last did.

body.description: The body whose surface gravity (and, at the surface, pressure) to use; defaults to the body the craft is at.

situation.description: vacuum, or surface for the body's sea-level pressure.

name: plan_ascent
description: Flies the launch block's ascent from this turn's Game Snapshot (stage figures, the craft's nose-first drag) for turn_shape 0.20 to 0.80 and gives the one reaching target_ap and orbit with the most delta-v left; or reaches_orbit false naming the Boost stage that falls. Per stage: its role (Boost stage if it lights suborbital, else Orbital stage) and the altitude, speed, apoapsis, periapsis and time to apoapsis when it lights; then delta-v to orbit, left and kept by stage_limit, and the margin (marginal when thin). Give turn_shape to fly one shape. Its block is launch: pass launch the turn_shape it gives, with the same target_ap, stage_limit, turn_start_speed and throttle_max_q. target_lan or launch_at adds launch_ut, heading. A point-mass sim, not KSP. Don't call it for a body without air (use stage_performance), or again when the craft and target_ap haven't changed since you last did.

target_ap.description: Apoapsis to reach, m, or "auto" (the atmosphere top + 10 km), as launch.

stage_limit.description: As the blocks: the launch never stages below it (default 0).

target_inc.description: Inclination, degrees, as launch (default 0): how much of the body's turning helps.

target_lan.description: LAN, degrees: also gives the launch window into target_inc and it.

launch_at.description: A moon's name: the window into its plane (as launch).

turn_shape.description: Fly this shape only instead of searching.

name: find_landing_site
description: Up to 3 landing sites on an airless body that the craft's current orbit passes over within a window, from the game's live terrain, biome and sun: each has latitude and longitude (degrees), biome, terrain altitude (m above sea level), slope (degrees), the UT the ground track passes over it, the sun's elevation then, and landing_ut, when land would touch down there from this orbit (correction_dv: its burn onto the site, m/s). Only sites land can fly come back. Filters: an optional biome, daylight (defaults to the Mission Settings), a slope limit (default 5 degrees), a window in hours (defaults to the larger of the Mission Settings time cap and one turn of the body, at most 48) and an optional point to be near. The craft must orbit the body. Its block is land: call it to see that a biome target or a landing the Mission Goal names can be flown, instead of searching by hand, then pass land the biome with the site as near (or the site alone as its target), and any within_hours or max_correction_dv you gave here. plane_changes, for near (else the first site or the biome's): change_orbit calls (set_inc) that put it under the track, with plane_change_dv, landing_dv and total_dv: cheapest and soonest when land cannot reach it from this orbit, else one only if it saves 20 m/s net. Fly the one you pick as its own step before land, budgeting its total_dv. Don't call it for land's target "any", or for a body with an atmosphere (an error; deorbit aims those landings).

body.description: The airless body to land on, which the craft is orbiting.

biome.description: Only sites in this biome (e.g. Highlands, Midlands, Poles); omit for any.

daylight.description: Only sites in Daylight when the track passes: the sun more than 20 degrees above the horizon; defaults to the Mission Settings.

max_slope_deg.description: The steepest ground allowed, degrees; default 5.

within_hours.description: How far ahead to look along the ground track, hours (at most 48); defaults to the larger of the Mission Settings time cap and one turn of the body.

max_correction_dv.description: The most land's correction burn onto a site may cost, m/s; defaults to land's: the smaller of 30 and 5% of the craft's delta-v.

edge_margin_m.description: With a biome: how far inside its edge a site should be, m; default 5000 (about the landing accuracy), 0 for none. Sites at the edge come back only when nothing deeper is reachable, marked near_biome_edge.

near.description: Prefer sites close to this point, degrees (within 15 degrees of arc of it); plane_changes are for it.

name: plan_transfer
description: The cheapest two-burn transfer in the next window, from this turn's Game Snapshot: to target (a body orbiting the craft's body) at target_pe (m), or to orbit (ap, pe m; inc, lan deg) anywhere on it. Gives the departure burn (maneuver-node components) and time, and the arrival burn; capture false minimises the departure alone. Its block is transfer_to: call it to budget a transfer, then pass the block the target. Don't call it for another planet's moons.

name: propose_mission_plan
description: Only for a request that asks for a Mission Plan; never a placeholder or a first step on any other request, which you reply to directly. Hand in your Mission Plan. The mod answers ok, or the problems to fix before you call it again. Then reply with kind mission_plan: the plan is the last one it accepted in this turn.

goal_steps.description: The Mission Goal as a few short steps, in order; each Debrief ticks them by number.

child_vessels.description: The Child Vessels you plan to fly, each named once; separated vessels not named here are ignored.

name.description: Your name for it, used as the vessel of its sequences.

separation_stage.description: The separation stage that releases it, from the separations facts; -1 for one already separated.

vessel_id.description: For a vessel already separated, its id from the mod's notice; otherwise empty.

vessel.description: craft, or the name of the Child Vessel this sequence flies.

due_time_ut.description: The Due Time as UT in seconds, only when the wait before this sequence needs the player (e.g. docking or an EVA by hand); otherwise -1. A wait for a window, daylight or a hold goes inside the sequence's script, which warps there.

manual.description: True for a stretch the player flies by hand.

mission_time_s.description: Expected total Mission time in seconds, waits between sequences included; -1 if you can't say.

new_goal.description: Only when the player asked to change the Mission Goal itself: the new Mission Goal in their words, which replaces the old one if they approve this plan; otherwise empty.
